panels.title: ABOUT
panels.text: An MCP server that gives AI coding agents a memory of your codebase and a sprint process. Your agents forget everything between sessions. This one file does not.

items.text: Gives AI coding agents **persistent memory**. The memory survives the session.
Indexes your codebase into one SQLite file, `context.db`. Agents query file roles, exports and dependents.

items.lead: Fewer tokens in real agent runs
items.text: On import-graph questions (683-file fixture, n=5) it used 28-47 % fewer uncached tokens (GLM 5.3 and DeepSeek v4 pro; DeepSeek cost -29 %) at equal or better success, every repeat above 0. With Claude Code (Opus) on two tasks it used more. The 43.7 % figure is simulated: see the benchmark in 04 USAGE.
Runs a full sprint process for a 9-agent team: vision, discovery, milestones, epics, tickets, gates and retros. It uses 97 MCP tools and 6 slash commands.
Shows everything on a live React dashboard at `:3333`. Zero API keys.

`npm install vlm-code-context-mcp`. Zero API keys. One `context.db` file. Two entry points: `code-context` is the code index (6 tools, the default). `code-context-sprint` adds the sprint process and the dashboard on the same database.

`npx code-context-mcp setup .` creates `context.db`, indexes your codebase and installs `code-context-sprint`. It seeds a 9-agent team and the frontend skill library into the project database. `--profile code` installs `code-context` instead.
Setup writes `.mcp.json`. It offers to wire the sprint statusline into `.claude/settings.json`. Pass `--defaults` to skip the prompts.
It switches to **update mode**: migrate (with automatic backup) and config repair. It never touches your data. `--force` renames the old database. It does not delete it.
Claude Code (or any MCP client) loads the server from `.mcp.json`. Verify with `get_project_status`. Manual registration instead: see MANUAL SETUP in 04 USAGE.
`npx code-context-dashboard ./context.db` opens at `http://localhost:3333` with live SSE updates.

File watching and auto-reindex on save are on by default (derived from the indexed files). Pass a directory as the 4th argument only to override it, for example on a database with nothing indexed yet: `npx code-context-dashboard ./context.db 3333 .`

Type `/kickoff` in Claude Code. The orchestrator walks you through vision -> discovery -> milestone -> epics -> tickets -> sprint -> implementation -> retro. It asks one question at a time. Smart resume lets you stop and continue later.

rows.text: Context efficiency from scripted replays. No model runs. This is the source of the 43.7 % figure (simulated, 2026-10-11).

A real model, the same task in three arms: without the server, with it, and with it plus the instruction to use it first. Task sets L1-L6 (sample project and this repo) and I1-I6 (generated 683-file fixture).
Pre-registered external harness (Claude Code sessions). Read-only.

items.text: Success vanilla / cc / guided: 6/8 · 6/8 · 7/8. Uncached tokens saved: cc **+11.2 %**, guided **+15.4 %** (n=1, no range). Cost saved cc / guided: +7.9 % / +13.5 %. Uncached tokens per PASS: 10,070 · 8,946 · 7,306.
Real agent numbers from proof runs on 2026-10-11, rescored and renormalized. "Saved" compares each arm with vanilla (no server); positive means fewer. Range = min .. max over repeats.
Small n, fixed fixtures (L1/L2 sample project, L4/L6 this repo, I-tasks the generated fixture), one day. The guided DeepSeek miss is an L6 timeout (300 s).
GLM caches tool definitions across sessions with no off switch, so its uncached counts leave out that prefix.
opus-20261011-134112: n=2 per task and arm (one cold, one warm), no guided arm. opus-20261011-145449: 8 tasks, n=1, no range. The two runs disagree on the sign. Read both as indicative.
The bench verdict compares each arm with vanilla. A success drop of more than 5 points is SUBOPTIMAL, also when the tokens go down. glm-20261011-184607 is SUBOPTIMAL for this reason.
Agent runs before 2026-10-11 00:00 UTC told every arm to use the built-in file tools. They do not show the server in use.

items.text: **Frontend** (22 skills plus an editable house-style primer), **Landing pages** and **Workflow**.
The MCP server serves them into your live session. They are not copied into your repo.
[claude_development_skills](https://github.com/VelimirMueller/claude_development_skills), vendored under `vendor/skills/`.
The project DB `skills` table (`fe:*`, `la:*`, `wf:*`). Edit them. Re-seeds never overwrite your edits.
`/kickoff` asks once. `update_skill_sets({ landing: true, ... })` changes it any time.
`CODE_CONTEXT_SKILLS_AUTOSYNC=1` syncs from the latest upstream release at boot. `pnpm run sync:skills` re-vendors the offline fallback.
`/kickoff` loads the frontend skill playbook into the session when a sprint has `fe-engineer` work.

rows.text: Node.js 22 or newer, 24 LTS recommended. Build: TypeScript strict mode.

Exports and import edges for TypeScript/JavaScript, Python and PHP (classes, interfaces, traits, enums, functions, constants; `use` statements resolved through `composer.json` PSR-4 maps). Other files are indexed with a summary only.
SQLite via better-sqlite3, WAL mode. 33 tables (27 scrum + 6 code).
@modelcontextprotocol/sdk. The server sends short MCP `instructions` (about 90 tokens) on when to use the graph tools.
React 19 + Vite + Zustand + Framer Motion. CSS variables + Tailwind, dark theme. 75 React components.
SSE via WAL file watcher.
Vitest. 2423 backend tests and 142 dashboard tests.
9 agent roles (configurable). 4 sprint phases with gate checks + planning gate. 6 slash commands.

7: `code-context` (index), `code-context-sprint` (sprint process), `code-context-mcp` (setup), `code-context-dashboard`, `code-context-statusline`, `code-context-reindex`, `code-context-sync-github`. Alias: `vlm-code-context-mcp` = `code-context`.

readme.hero_alt: code-context-mcp. Read less. Know more. Stable, v3.0.0. MCP, code index, sprints, dashboard.

code:
# Requires Node.js 22 or newer. Node.js 24 LTS is recommended.
npm install vlm-code-context-mcp

# The code index (default): 6 tools
npx code-context-reindex . --db ./context.db
claude mcp add code-context -- npx code-context ./context.db

# Or the sprint process instead: setup installs code-context-sprint, /kickoff, the dashboard
npx code-context-mcp setup .
npx code-context-dashboard ./context.db   # optional: live dashboard on :3333

# override the watch directory (4th argument)
npx code-context-dashboard ./context.db 3333 .

search_files("auth middleware")       → find the right file
get_file_context("src/auth.ts")      → understand role, exports, dependents
Read("src/auth.ts")                  → only now read the actual code

# Simulated (no model, no cost)
pnpm run bench

# Agent (real model, real tokens; needs ZAI_API_KEY or DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
pnpm run bench:live --provider glm

# Publish the run to the bench-results branch (rebuilds the site)
pnpm run bench:publish

# The code index (default), after npm install
claude mcp add code-context -- npx code-context ./context.db

# Or the sprint process instead (same server name, same context.db; includes the code tools)
claude mcp add code-context -- npx code-context-sprint ./context.db

# Without a local install (the index)
claude mcp add code-context -- npx -y vlm-code-context-mcp ./context.db

# Add globally (the index; dist/server/sprint.js for the sprint process)
claude mcp add --scope user code-context node /path/to/node_modules/vlm-code-context-mcp/dist/server/index.js ./context.db

# Remove
claude mcp remove code-context

# Profiles (default: code, 6 tools)
CODE_CONTEXT_PROFILE=full     # 97 tools: the sprint process (setup writes it)
CODE_CONTEXT_PROFILE=all      # 103 tools
CODE_CONTEXT_TOOLSETS=scrum   # add toolsets: code-admin, scrum, fun, stream

# Output
OVERDRIVE_FLAIR=0              # flair off (1 forces it on)
CODE_CONTEXT_TIMESTAMPS=1      # add modified/indexed timestamps
CODE_CONTEXT_ABSOLUTE_PATHS=1  # absolute paths

# Skills
CODE_CONTEXT_SKILLS_AUTOSYNC=1 # sync skills from upstream at boot

# Contributors use pnpm (pnpm-lock.yaml); install once
pnpm install

# MCP server
pnpm run dev

# Dashboard (Vite dev server with HMR)
pnpm run dashboard:dev

# Tests
pnpm test          # backend
pnpm run test:all  # backend + frontend

# Maintainers: publish to the npm registry (runs prepublishOnly = pnpm run build)
pnpm publish
